findings.message: ADDITIONAL_HF_REPOS is now a required config key, so an existing catalog whose config.yaml lacks it (or has one malformed entry) now fails config validation as a whole, and the site falls back to empty defaults and shows no catalog at all. main.js:765-766 pushes 'ADDITIONAL_HF_REPOS (must be a list)' when the key is absent, and lines 769-774 do the same for any bad entry. Line 782 then throws, and the catch at 792-799 replaces the whole CONFIG with ORGANIZATION_NAME: ''. The guard at main.js:897 ('if (!ORGANIZATION_NAME) return;') then stops the data loading. Before this change, a config without the key loaded normally. This repo is a template ('Welcome to your new catalog repo', README), so downstream catalogs that pick up the new main.js without editing their config.yaml hit this. Treating a missing key as [] would keep them working.

The PR says ADDITIONAL_HF_REPOS is optional and defaults to [] when it's missing. The code doesn't do that. A missing key is pushed into `missing`, which throws a config error. The catch block then swaps the whole user config for the hard-coded defaults, including ORGANIZATION_NAME: ''. So any existing catalog (this is a template repo) whose config.yaml lacks the new key would show a configuration error and an empty catalog after this update. Default it when absent, e.g. `CONFIG.ADDITIONAL_HF_REPOS ??= []`, and only fail validation when the key is present but malformed. export-tags.js now throws for any config.yaml that lacks ADDITIONAL_HF_REPOS, so the dev script stops working on existing configs even though the feature is optional. export-tags.js:48-52 says 'if (!Array.isArray(CONFIG.ADDITIONAL_HF_REPOS)) throw new Error(...)'. The requiredKeys list at line 32 and the header comment at line 11 don't mention the new key, so the script's documented contract and its behaviour disagree.

Same contradiction as in main.js: the PR says the key is optional, but this throws when ADDITIONAL_HF_REPOS is absent. Existing configs without the key would break `node scripts/export-tags.js`. Two config entries that name the same HF repo with different letter case are both fetched and both added, so the same repo can appear twice in the catalog. Deduplication at main.js:304-308 compares the raw entry.repo strings ('seenRepos.has(entry.repo)'), and line 326 filters only against existingIds, which holds the org listing alone. Hugging Face resolves repo paths case-insensitively and returns the canonical id. So 'User/x' and 'user/x' both get past seenRepos, both come back with id 'user/x', and both are appended. The same logic is in scripts/export-tags.js:127-139.

Deduplication is an exact string match on entry.repo, and fetched items are only checked against the org's existingIds, not against each other. Hugging Face repo IDs are case-insensitive, so two config entries that differ only in case (or one with trailing whitespace) are both fetched and appended. That produces duplicate cards. Also, entry.repo is validated with .trim() but the raw value goes into the URL. Dedupe the fetched items by their canonical item.id, and trim/normalise repo before building the URL. Each additional model is fetched from the same endpoint twice per page load: once in the new block, then again in the existing per-model detail step. The new code fetches `${API_BASE_URL}${repoType}/${entry.repo}` (line 312), which for models is `${API_BASE_URL}models/<id>`. It appends the result to hfItems, and the existing Step 2 at line 332 then fetches `${API_BASE_URL}models/${item.id}` for every item in hfItems, including those just fetched.

Additional model repos are fetched from `${API_BASE_URL}models/${repo}`. They are merged into hfItems, and Step 2 then fetches `models/${item.id}` again for every item. Each additional model costs two identical requests. Skip the detail fetch for items that already came from the per-repo endpoint, or add the additional models after Step 2. No tests cover the new behaviour: merging extra repos per type, skipping duplicates, tolerating failed fetches, and validating config entries. The diff touches only README.md, main.js, public/config.yaml and scripts/export-tags.js. A glob for *.test.* / *.spec.* in the export finds no test files, so none of the new branches (main.js:300-327 and 765-775) is checked by anything automated.

In the tag-export script, a failed fetch of an additional HF repo is dropped silently, so a typo in a repo name leaves its tags out of tag-export.txt with no warning. export-tags.js:134-136 uses `get(...).then(({ json }) => json).catch(() => null)` with no logging. The browser version at main.js:315 and 321 calls console.warn for the same failure.

Unlike main.js, this swallows failed fetches of additional HF repos with `.catch(() => null)` and logs nothing. A typo in a repo name or type in ADDITIONAL_HF_REPOS silently drops those tags from the export. Log a warning that names the failing repo. The new validation message puts JSON.stringify of config entries into the error banner, which is rendered with innerHTML, so markup in a config value is interpreted as HTML. Line 773 adds `bad entries: ${badEntries.map(e => JSON.stringify(e)).join(', ')}` to the message. main.js:788 renders it with `errorDiv.innerHTML = `Configuration Error: ${error.message}...``. The input is owner-controlled config, so impact is limited.

Bad entries are JSON.stringify'd into the error message, which is then put into the page via `errorDiv.innerHTML` (line 788). Config values such as `` would be rendered as HTML. config.yaml is usually trusted, but use textContent for the message, or escape it. entry.repo goes into the API URL unencoded and is only checked for being a non-empty string, so a value with '?', '#' or '../' would request a different API path than intended. main.js:312 builds `${API_BASE_URL}${repoType}/${entry.repo}`, and validation at line 770 checks only `typeof e.repo !== 'string' || !e.repo.trim()`, with no owner/name format check. The value comes from the site owner's config, so the risk is low. The same applies to scripts/export-tags.js:134.

The validation rules and the fetch-and-merge logic for additional HF repos are copied between main.js and scripts/export-tags.js, so the two can drift apart, and already differ in how they log errors. export-tags.js:53-61 repeats main.js:768-774 nearly word for word, and export-tags.js:123-140 repeats main.js:300-327.
